chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, all of them, from Safwan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a female slave who belongs to a man, whom he circles (for intimacy), and she goes out and becomes pregnant. He said: 'The man is suspected (of being the father), or his family is suspected.' I said: 'As for an apparent suspicion, no (it is not just suspicion).' He said: 'Then the child is established (as his).'

key_terms.يَتَّهِمُهَا: He is suspected (of being the father)
key_terms.يُطِيفُ بِهَا: He circles her (referring to sexual intercourse)

ai.seo_question: How is paternity established for a child born to a male owner's female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of *lhuq al-awlād* (attribution of lineage), establishing that a master's sexual intimacy with his female slave (*jitāya*) creates a presumption of paternity unless a specific defect or impediment is proven. It highlights the scholarly distinction between general suspicion and clear evidence, ensuring the child's lineage is secured for inheritance and social status, a principle deeply rooted in the Imams' legal reasoning.
